query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but its poor oxygen resistance limits practical high-temperature use. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing the alloy’s useful mechanical performance? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention and mechanism, the predicted change relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr, the relevant temperature, atmosphere, exposure time, and mechanical-loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Aluminum oxide (Al2O3) coating on Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr can improve its oxygen resistance without sacrificing mechanical performance.
generation.intervention: Deposition of 1-2 μm thick Al2O3 coating using plasma spray technique
generation.conditions: Temperature: 1000 °C, Atmosphere: Air, Exposure time: 100 hours, Mechanical-loading boundaries: Strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1
generation.mechanism: Formation of a protective oxide layer that prevents oxygen diffusion into the alloy, reducing oxidation and degradation
generation.predicted_outcome: 20-30% increase in room-temperature tensile ductility and 10-20% increase in yield strength at 1000 °C, relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr
generation.uncertainty: The actual performance of the Al2O3 coating may vary depending on the deposition technique, coating thickness, and surface roughness of the substrate

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Al2O3-coated sample shows less than 10% improvement in room-temperature tensile ductility or less than 5% improvement in yield strength at 1000 °C, compared to the untreated sample, after 100 hours of exposure to air at 1000 °C, then the hypothesis is falsified
